newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says will not rely on fiscal spending.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says will not rely on fiscal spending.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday that Japan will not depend on fiscal spending as a measure to stimulate its economy.
He told a news conference that Japan will deregulate its economy to achieve economic growth led by domestic demand.
Hashimoto made the remarks after his cabinet approved fiscal reform plans which call for a 0.5 percent cut in the fiscal 1998/99 budget from the current budget.

Asked if the plan not to use fiscal spending to stimulate the economy runs counter to a U.S. request to expand Japan's domestic demand with additional fiscal spending, Hashimoto said: "The fiscal reform plan will bring about an increase in domestic demand over the medium and long term".
Washington has argued that Japan should expand its economic growth so as to absorb more imports to help cut its trade deficit with the United States.
Hashimoto added that Japan's surplus in trade and services will not expand to a level which will hurt Tokyo's stable relations with Washington unless there are extreme fluctuations in exchange rates.

Hashimoto said the fiscal reform plans approved on Tuesday will help the government achieve a target of bringing down the fiscal deficit to less than three percent of gross domestic product by fiscal 2003.
"Without fiscal reform, we cannot have the prospect of a revitalised society in the 21st century," Hashimoto said.
